paper_title: TRIC: A Thermal Resistance and Impedance Calculator for Electronic Packages

scenario.description: Thermal impedance ZTHJA vs. time of a 10 × 10 mm² eTQFP with a 6 × 6 mm² epad for four different die sizes (2×2, 3×3, 4×4, 5×5 mm²), dissipating 1 W via a power step applied at t=0
scenario.architecture: 10×10 mm² eTQFP package; 6×6 mm² exposed pad; rectangular parallelepiped mesh; Manhattan geometry; epad lead frame with depressed die pad; leads extending from all four sides; single heat source on die
scenario.workload: Power step: 1 W applied instantaneously at t=0 to single heat source; uniform power distribution over die surface; junction-to-ambient (ϑJA) thermal path; static conditions reached at approximately 400 s
scenario.operating_point: Transient thermal response from t=10⁻⁵ s to t=10³ s; ambient temperature Tamb=20°C (inferred from Section 4.3); junction temperature rise over ambient normalized to 1 W input power; no active cooling beyond natural convection

original_setup.solver: Finite Volume (FV) method based; TRIC uses model-order reduction (MOR) with multigrid iterative solver for complex frequency domain equations
original_setup.optimizer: Projection-based approach (Algorithms 1-3); parametric model-order reduction without traditional optimization
original_setup.controller: None; passive thermal system with boundary conditions defined per JEDEC ambient specifications
original_setup.benchmark: FloTHERM v12.2 (Mentor Graphics) for validation; JEDEC thermal metrics (ϑJA, ΨJB, ΨJCtop, ϑJB, ϑJCtop, ϑJCbottom)

thermal_observable.aggregation: point measurement at die center or heat source center; thermal impedance ZTHJA = ϑJA(t) defined as temperature rise normalized to applied power

physical_mismatches.reason: TRIC is a compact thermal model extraction tool, not a direct thermal simulation of actual packaged devices; relies on simplified Manhattan geometry pDTMs with aggregate properties (e.g., weighted-average lead thermal conductivity) rather than explicit die, lead, and mold geometry

Boundary conditions are idealized per JEDEC standards (e.g., extremely high heat transfer coefficient on bottom surface for ϑJCbottom) rather than realistic thermal interface materials or mounting conditions
No transient heat generation profile data provided for the eTQFP scenario; Figure 6 uses artificial power step input (1 W step at t=0) not representative of actual semiconductor operation
Multi-source analysis (Section 4.4) considers only static layouts with fixed heat source positions; does not model dynamic power distribution or thermal coupling feedback during transient operation

studio_assumptions: Purely conductive heat transfer (no convection or radiation explicitly modeled within package); convection implicit in boundary conditions
Board modeled as single finely-meshed parallelepiped with adjusted thermal conductivity to represent aggregate metal traces and vias
Pins and leads represented as single rectangular parallelepiped with weighted-average thermal conductivity (not detailed geometry)
Die attach material properties assumed constant; glue type selectable but properties not explicitly documented
Steady-state and transient solutions derived from linear thermal resistance/capacitance network via projection onto reduced basis
Intrinsic package symmetry exploited: only quarter-structure meshed with adiabatic boundary conditions on symmetry planes
Non-Manhattan variations (e.g., pLQFP die position shift with thickness change, multi-source die layouts) handled via geometric coordinate transformation and projection basis adaptation
Mesh convergence: discretization chosen to achieve ≤0.1% inaccuracy based on prior convergence study (reference [11])
missing_inputs: Exact mesh dimensions (nx, ny, nz grid points) and timestep refinement (nt values) for Figure 6 transient simulation not provided
Detailed material thermal conductivity and heat capacity values for die, epad, mold, board, and lead/pin materials not tabulated in paper
Die thickness value for Figure 6 scenario not explicitly stated (paper mentions 100, 280, 375, 580 µm options for eLQFPs but does not specify which was used)
Heat source power profile details beyond power step; no clock frequency, dynamic power scaling, or realistic IC workload model documented
TRIC source code, executable, or supplementary material repository not linked in paper; Figure 2 shows DTM meshes but no CAD or mesh files provided
Ambient temperature explicitly stated as 20°C only in Section 4.3 context; not universally specified for all scenarios
JEDEC standard reference (JESD51-12) cited but full boundary condition specification details not reproduced in paper
FloTHERM v12.2 setup and mesh parameters for comparison runs not detailed; mesh style differences mentioned as cause of ~3% discrepancy but specific mesh counts and refinement criteria not disclosed
